brief.text:
ENDOCRINE INSIGHT REPORT

OBSERVED PATTERNS
1. Symptom clustering: 13 of 16 fatigue logs fell on cycle days 20–28, across 4 of 4 cycles observed.
2. Laboratory measurements: Day-21 progesterone 7.9 → 4.2 ng/mL (Aug 1 vs Sep 26); Day-21 estradiol 132 → 141 pg/mL (Aug 1 vs Sep 26), stable; Day-25 TSH 2.6 → 2.4 mIU/L (Jul 8 vs Sep 2), stable; iron/ferritin and B12 not measured in the last 91 days.
3. Medication timing: Fatigue logs rose from 5 in the 46 days before starting Spironolactone 50 mg (Aug 16) to 11 in the 45 days after.
4. Sleep: On nights outside cycle days 20–28, average sleep went from 7.2 h before Aug 16 to 6.9 h after; late-luteal nights averaged 6.1 h vs 7.0 h on other nights.

SYSTEM INTERPRETATION
3 factors are temporally associated with the fatigue pattern. Your cycle is the most consistent signal; the medication change and a lab change are also associated. Sleep changed too, and no specialist owned it, so it stays an open confounder.

QUESTIONS FOR MY CLINICIAN
• Could the timing of my fatigue relative to my cycle be relevant?
• Could Spironolactone 50 mg be contributing to my fatigue?
• Should my day-21 progesterone values be evaluated together with these symptoms?
• Would iron/ferritin or B12 testing be useful for me?
